d: A continuous six-to-eight hour simulation with no player and no winning state. Five Ghosts — a gatekeeper who sells access to land permits, a cult leader who reads fortune for speculators, a developer building European castles in empty fields, a central bank that speaks only in figures, and a narrator who turns every rise and fall into a story — wager against one another inside an invented city of construction booms, credit injections and promised transformation. Each Ghost hosts a table where the others bet, and each adjusts its strategy from what it loses. Nothing is authored frame by frame; hierarchies, debts and collapses emerge from betting behaviour. The structure borrows from resource simulation and from roguelike: cycles repeat, difficulty compounds, and a prestige mechanic resets the world so it can boom and fall again.
c:
With Áng Mây Huyền Diệu.
Real-time simulation, generative sound.
Duration 6–8 hours, continuous.

d: Chia takes decentralisation as a working method rather than a subject. The question is not what a group can make together, but what it takes to make anything at all without a centre — and whether that is possible without either dissolving into informality or quietly re-forming a boss. The Vietnamese verb names several acts at once: chia bài, to deal cards; chia phần, to divide a finite share; chia việc, to divide labour; chia sẻ, to share as giving; chia rẽ, to split a group against itself. Sharing a burden and breaking a group apart are the same word with a different tail. Independent art in Vietnam is not centralised, it is ad hoc: roles unspoken, contracts rare, things made because someone stayed up. Credit accrues to whoever is most visible; labour to whoever cares most. Neither is anyone's decision, which is why neither can be contested. The project holds one narrow question: how little structure is required to keep the ad hoc from becoming extractive?
A group exhibition held in a private residence in Hanoi, August 2025.

d: An experimental and dance set by NetChùa!, with original arrangements by Nananarc, Xcerpt and Quản Huyền, followed by a mini DJ set from Lưu Dạ Hưng. The set draws on the daily lives and memories of ordinary Vietnamese people: karaoke, Vietnam Airlines, real estate, TikTok voiceovers, and a shared frustration with curatorial word salad.

d: A group exhibition. THOẢ holds a cluster of Vietnamese compounds at once — thoả mãn, to satisfy; thoả thuận, to agree; thoả hiệp, to compromise; thoả ước, to fulfil a wish. Each work settles somewhere in that range: what an artist satisfies, concedes, or agrees to in order to make anything at all. Presented with 34 Studio, within baybyhung's field. Visitors were asked to bring headphones.
c:

d: A grassroots platform for art, knowledge sharing and gaming, which treats internet cafes as low-cost multi-functional cultural spaces. Events run on-site and simultaneously via netchua.live, so artists and audiences can take part from anywhere. NetChùa! treats the experiment in experimental as a verb: it prioritises learning, cooperation and exchange over competition, and encourages methods that bypass the pursuit of excellence, social acceptance and seniority. It operates non-profit and donation-only, publishes its income and expenses, and shares revenue back in equal parts.
c:
Hanoi, VN. Ongoing, from 2026.
Team: Xcerpt, Nananarc, Quản Huyền, Mieke, angmayhuyendieu, Whoopzy, Lưu Dạ Hưng.
Collaborators: Tàu Hũ Ky Collective, Chữ Cháy.

d: 34 Studio works across materials without ranking them: steel, ceramic, cloth, sound, light, code and the body pass through the same process. A project is built, shown and dismantled inside one address — the workshop is also the exhibition floor and the stage. It is not a gallery and keeps no permanent collection; what it keeps is the working record — process notes, test footage, failed casts, the versions that did not hold — consulted to decide what to try next, not to reissue. It began in 2021 because Hanoi had no infrastructure for work that resists category, so the studio took on the whole chain itself: production, presentation, documentation, and paying the people involved. Collaborators are chosen for making the studio slightly uncomfortable; comfort is a reliable sign of repetition.
c:
Hanoi, VN. Ongoing, from 2021.
Artists: Đan, Thành, Hoàng, Ngọc, Hưng (@baybyhung).
